item.text: The shared decode hook currently splits on commas. I’ll replace it with a hook limited to string inputs and `[]string` targets, then cover YAML, ENV, empty strings, and YAML sequences.

 var decodeHooks = mapstructure.ComposeDecodeHookFunc(
 	mapstructure.StringToTimeDurationHookFunc(),
-	mapstructure.StringToSliceHookFunc(","),
+	stringToSliceHookFunc(),
 	stringToEnumHookFunc(stringToLogEncoding),
 	stringToEnumHookFunc(stringToCacheBackend),
 	stringToEnumHookFunc(stringToScheme),

 )
 
+// stringToSliceHookFunc splits scalar strings into string slices on whitespace.
+func stringToSliceHookFunc() mapstructure.DecodeHookFuncType {
+	return func(from reflect.Type, to reflect.Type, data interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
+		if from.Kind() != reflect.String || to != reflect.TypeOf([]string{}) {
+			return data, nil
+		}
+

+	}

+func TestAllowedOriginsFromScalar(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name  string
+		value string
+		want  []string
+	}{
+		{name: "spaces", value: "foo.com bar.com  baz.com", want: []string{"foo.com", "bar.com", "baz.com"}},
+		{name: "mixed whitespace", value: " \tfoo.com\nbar.com  \t baz.com\n", want: []string{"foo.com", "bar.com", "baz.com"}},
+		{name: "empty", value: "", want: []string{}},
+		{name: "only whitespace", value: " \t\n ", want: []string{}},
+	}
+
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			path := t.TempDir() + "/config.yml"
+			content := fmt.Sprintf("cors:\n  allowed_origins: %q\n", tt.value)
+			require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0600))
+
+			t.Run("YAML", func(t *testing.T) {
+				cfg, err := Load(path)
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				assert.Equal(t, tt.want, cfg.Cors.AllowedOrigins)
+			})
+
+			t.Run("ENV", func(t *testing.T) {
+				t.Setenv("FLIPT_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS", tt.value)
+				cfg, err := Load("./testdata/default.yml")
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				assert.Equal(t, tt.want, cfg.Cors.AllowedOrigins)
+			})
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestStringToSliceHookOnlyConvertsStringsToStringSlices(t *testing.T) {
+	hook := stringToSliceHookFunc()
+	stringSlice := reflect.TypeOf([]string{})
+
+	for _, tt := range []struct {
+		name string
+		data interface{}
+		to   reflect.Type
+	}{
+		{name: "sequence", data: []string{"foo.com", "bar.com"}, to: stringSlice},
+		{name: "number", data: 42, to: stringSlice},
+		{name: "other target", data: "foo.com bar.com", to: reflect.TypeOf([]int{})},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			got, err := hook(reflect.TypeOf(tt.data), tt.to, tt.data)
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			assert.Equal(t, tt.data, got)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestAllowedOriginsFromYAMLSequence(t *testing.T) {

+}

item.text: The hook and tests are in place. The package test is still running; it will check empty scalar values as well as whitespace parsing, since Viper may handle empty ENV values differently.

The test found that Viper ignores an empty ENV value and falls back to the `"*"` default. I enabled empty ENV values so the decode hook receives `""`; the config package tests now pass. I’ll review the final diff for scope and formatting.

item.text:
Updated [config.go](/app/internal/config/config.go) so scalar strings decode into `[]string` using whitespace as the separator. This handles repeated, leading, and trailing whitespace and produces an empty slice for an empty string. YAML sequences remain unchanged, and empty ENV values now reach the decoder.

Added YAML and ENV coverage and updated the advanced config fixture. `go test ./internal/config` and `git diff --check` pass.
